patients.summary: Retired construction worker with hypertension and HFpEF who joined in 2020; actinic keratoses, presbycusis with hearing aids, a low-grade bladder urothelial carcinoma resected in 2023, and a stage IB right upper lobe adenocarcinoma treated with SBRT in 2024. Statin-associated muscle symptoms on rechallenge, an ADHF admission in 2025, and amaurosis fugax from a 50-69% right ICA stenosis managed medically.

documents.title: New patient call

documents.body: Caller is Mr. Talbot, 65, on Medicare. Says his old office keeps cancelling on him and a neighbor recommended us. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. He wants to go ahead. Booked new patient visit 9/22 at 9:00. Asked him to bring all pill bottles and the name of the old office so we can request records. Release form mailed.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 y/o retired construction worker transferring care; brought a bag of bottles.

HPI: Long-standing high blood pressure and what his last doctor called heart failure, diagnosed a few years back after he got winded and puffy; he thinks he had an ultrasound of the heart then. Weighs himself 'when I remember.' No orthopnea or PND now, walks the block without stopping, ankles fine. Knees ache on stairs and after yard work, both sides, for years; doesn't take anything for it. Treated for TB about 18 years ago, finished the pills, no problems since. Had pneumonia this past February, treated with antibiotics at the old office, felt back to normal within a few weeks.

Meds (verified from bottles): lisinopril 20 daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, HCTZ 25 daily, furosemide 40 qAM, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily.
Allergies: none to drugs.
PSH: none.
FHx: father MI at 62. Mother HTN and type 2 DM. Brother high cholesterol.
Social: divorced, lives alone, daughter nearby and checks on him. Smoked about a pack a day for 40 years, quit in 2012. 1-2 beers a week. Retired from construction.

Exam: well appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. JVP not elevated. No peripheral edema. Knees with crepitus, no effusion, full ROM. Skin: weathered, sun-damaged face and forearms.

A/P:
1. HTN - at goal today on current regimen. BMP.
2. Chronic heart failure, sounds like preserved EF - asked for the echo with old records. Euvolemic. Daily weights reviewed.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorva 40 - lipids today.
4. Knee OA - activity as tolerated.
5. Remote treated TB, recent pneumonia - records requested.
6. HM: HCV/HIV once today. Colonoscopy he thinks 2017, will confirm. Lung cancer screening eligible (40 pk-yr, quit 8 yrs ago) - discuss next visit. Flu shot at nurse visit next month.
RTC ~4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Talbot, your bloodwork from yesterday looks good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on your water pills, blood counts are normal, and your cholesterol is in a reasonable range on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes. See you in January.

reports.text: Outside study, prior office. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. LVEF estimated 55%. Impaired LV relaxation pattern on mitral inflow. Right ventricle normal size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Preserved LV systolic function, LVEF 55%. Impaired relaxation. No significant valve disease.

reports.text: Outside study, prior office. Follow-up after pneumonia. Lungs clear. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size within normal limits.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 38 pages received by fax from prior PCP office. Includes: problem list (HTN, heart failure, high cholesterol, knee arthritis, history of TB), med list matching ours, 2019 echocardiogram (EF 55%, impaired relaxation), February 2020 office notes for pneumonia treated with oral antibiotics, March 2020 follow-up chest x-ray clear, 2017 colonoscopy report (normal, repeat 10 years), Tdap 2017. Scanned. Flagged for PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old records reviewed. Echo 2019 EF 55% with impaired relaxation - fits HFpEF, problem list updated. Pneumonia Feb 2020 resolved, CXR clear 3/2020. Colonoscopy 2017 normal, next 2027. Tdap 2017.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu given L deltoid. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, waited 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: 90-day refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy asking to switch all six of his maintenance meds to 90-day supplies under the PCP. Sent lisinopril, metoprolol tartrate, HCTZ, furosemide, atorvastatin x 90 days with 3 refills. Aspirin is OTC.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for BP/HF check. Feels fine, shoveling with breaks. Weight steady on his bathroom scale. No SOB at night, no swelling.
Meds unchanged, taking them.
Exam: lungs clear, RRR, no JVD, no edema.
A/P: HTN controlled. HFpEF euvolemic. Continue all.
Lung cancer screening: 40 pack-years, quit 2012, age 65. Talked through what a yearly low-dose CT can find, false positives, radiation, and that a finding could mean more tests. He wants it. Ordered.
RTC spring for wellness visit.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening, former smoker, 40 pack-years. Technique: low-dose noncontrast CT of the chest. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your screening CT of the lungs was clear, nothing concerning. We'll repeat it in a year.

documents.body: Patient dropped off a copy of his vaccine card from the county clinic: Pfizer doses 2/9/21 and 3/2/21. Entered into immunization history.

orders.reason: one-time AAA screening, male former smoker 65-75

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial AWV.
Functional: independent in all ADLs/IADLs, drives, does his own shopping. No falls this year. Hearing: says it's 'fine.' Vision: readers only.
Mood: PHQ-2 0. Alcohol: AUDIT-C 1.
Cognition: Mini-Cog not needed, conversation intact, manages his own pills.
Advance directive: daughter is health care proxy, form given to complete.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2017 normal (next 2027). LDCT 1/2021 negative, next 1/2022. Flu 10/2020. COVID x2 done. Tdap 2017. Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines this fall. AAA ultrasound ordered (one time, ex-smoker).
First BP reading was up; better on repeat after sitting. No change. Lungs clear, no edema.
Labs: CMP, lipids.

reports.text: Limited aortic ultrasound for AAA screening. The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation and is normal in caliber throughout, maximal diameter 2.0 cm. Common iliac arteries normal caliber.

documents.title: Medication question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt asked whether he should skip the furosemide on hot days when he's working in the garden. Advised to keep taking it, drink to thirst, weigh daily, call if dizzy or weight drops more than a few pounds. He's fine with that.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Summer was busy with the garden. No dyspnea beyond baseline, no edema, weights 162-164 lb at home. Knees okay.
Exam: lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.
A/P: HTN and HFpEF stable, continue meds. BMP. Repeat screening CT ordered for January. Vaccines at nurse visit in October: flu, PCV20, COVID booster, start Shingrix.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Four vaccines given today per PCP order: high-dose flu L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid, COVID booster L deltoid (separated), Shingrix #1 R deltoid. Warned Shingrix can make him feel achy for a day or two. Observed 15 min. Shingrix #2 due in 2-6 months, booked 1/25.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not come in for 1:40. Called - said he got the dates mixed up and was at his daughter's. Since he was just seen in September, PCP fine to wait until spring wellness visit. Rebooked.
